transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 60 minutes
Location: All-hands (Zoom)
Attendees: David Turner (CEO), Maya Chen (CTO), Priya Nair (Head of Product), Liam O'Connor (Head of Engineering), Rachel Singh (Head of People), Omar Vasquez (VP Sales), plus ~120 staff joining.

Auto-generated Summary (may contain errors): Q4 close strong, passed 120M ARR milestone (spoken number may be rounded), Redwood Optimize beta in market, Dedicated sales momentum, a few big pilots for Private, holiday schedule, hiring pause in some teams, focus on reliability and on-call.

00:00:05 - David Turner: Hey everyone — good morning, good afternoon, wherever you are. Thanks for joining our December all-hands. I know it's a busy week with holidays coming up so we'll try to keep this tight. Quick agenda: Q4 results, product & roadmap, ops & people updates, then q's.

00:00:38 - Maya Chen: Good to see folks. I'll kick off with a short infra update before David walks through numbers. Engineering has been focused on latency SLOs and a big push on the KV cash — sorry K V cache, the transcription says K V cash sometimes — improvements that dropped median gen latency by about 12% on typical chat workloads. There are still some tail issues we're chasing.

00:01:12 - Liam O'Connor: Yeah, small note — the tail was most visible when customers use long context plus streaming, we tuned the batching policy and saw better throughput. We did a couple of kernel swaps for attention that helped on A100 and on the new AMP chips.

00:01:44 - David Turner: Great. On the business side we closed Q4 and hit an ARR milestone — the board was happy — we crossed roughly 120M ARR, rounding up. Big thanks to sales and product for a couple of enterprise deals on Dedicated. Omar, quick color?

00:02:05 - Omar Vasquez: Sure, we signed three mid-market and two enterprise Dedicated contracts this quarter. One of the enterprise customers moved from an incumbent after a performance benchmark we ran — they cared about predictable latency under load and the ability to run in their VPC. Security and audit logs won us that deal, along with the dedicated GPU pool SLA.

00:02:35 - Priya Nair: On product: we shipped Redwood Optimize beta to a handful of customers, which includes recommendations for batching, quant profiles, and cache hints. The initial feedback is positive — customers reduced token cost by ~18% in early runs. We'll open the beta to more customers next quarter.

00:03:06 - David Turner: Nice. A quick shoutout to the research/ML team for the quantization profiles work. Those profiles are a big lever for our cost story.

00:03:25 - Rachel Singh: People update — headcount: we're hiring in Sales and Solutions EM but pausing some individual IC hiring in core infra until Q1 unless there's a critical need. We'll be more deliberate on backfills. Holiday PTO: company closed Dec 24-25 and limited coverage Dec 31-Jan 1; detailed calendar to drop later today.

00:03:56 - David Turner: Thanks Rachel. Okay product roadmap brief — Priya?

00:04:08 - Priya Nair: H1 2027 priorities: 1) Make Private deployment GA for regulated customers with KMS/HSM integrations and longer retention for audit logs. 2) Improve Serving runtime perf — more kernel selections and sequence length aware routing. 3) A richer rollout system in Console: canaries, A/B and auto fallback. 4) Redwood Optimize to go from beta to standard add-on. We'll publish a full roadmap doc next week but those are the big bets.

00:04:52 - David Turner: On timing — Private GA target is end of Q1 2027, Redwood Optimize general availability targeted mid-Q2.

00:05:08 - Maya Chen: A technical note on Private: we've been testing VPC packaging and a self-hosted control plane; the recent e2e tests on customer infra hit a couple of edge cases with IAM mappings and SAML (transcribed as sam-el at times) that we fixed. The on-prem package also needs better disk-based cache eviction logic for low-memory hosts.

00:05:37 - Liam O'Connor: Also will call out that Dedicated autoscaling policies — we added a new burst capacity option for customers who have seasonal spikes, that helped one customer over Black Friday. Another improvement we rolled out is more transparent per-route latency breakdown in the Console.

00:06:05 - Omar Vasquez: On sales pipeline: big enterprise pilots in late stages — two are focused on Private (regulated finance and health), one is looking at Dedicated for global low-latency. We also see competitor activity — Vertex and Anthropic are pitching managed endpoints so we need to lean into our cost/throughput story.

00:06:36 - David Turner: Quick product demo snippets in the deck — Priya will share the deck later. Any big risks we should call out?

00:06:45 - Maya Chen: Reliability is top risk. We're tracking a handful of 95th/99th percentile latency incidents that correlate with GC and mem pressure in certain quant paths. We're on a 30 day action plan to close the largest regressions.

00:07:04 - Rachel Singh: On culture: small update — we launched a caregiver leave policy and new training for managers. Also reminding folks about the quarterly offsite plans for Feb — more details to come.

00:07:22 - David Turner: Open Q&A — please put questions in chat or raise hands.

00:07:30 - Employee 1 (Speaker): Hey David — congrats on ARR milestone. Quick question: is there any plan to expand regions in APAC early next year? Latency from APAC customers is still noisy.

00:07:44 - Omar Vasquez: We're prioritizing one APAC region for Q1 next year, partnering with a cloud vendor. The ask is mostly on data residency and lower tail latency.

00:08:01 - Employee 2 (Speaker): Regarding hiring pause — will ICs be at risk?

00:08:09 - Rachel Singh: Short answer: no mass layoffs planned. This is a targeted pause on new non-critical hiring. We're focused on reallocating headcount to high-leverage areas. We'll share more details with managers after this call.

00:08:24 - Employee 3 (Speaker): When is the Redwood Optimize rollout docs going live?

00:08:30 - Priya Nair: We'll publish the public beta guide and internal docs by 2026-12-08. Expect a sample workbook for cost regressions and a set of suggested quant profiles for common models.

00:08:45 - Employee 4 (Speaker): Could we get more transparency on runbooks for on-call?

00:08:50 - Liam O'Connor: We'll add a section in the Console runbook area that maps common alerts to runbooks and owners. Also working on better paging thresholds to reduce noise.

00:09:05 - David Turner: OK let's do a quick wins highlight — a few customer stories. Omar?

00:09:10 - Omar Vasquez: One customer, a healthcare platform, moved to Private because of audit log retention and KMS support. Their benchmark against our Dedicated offering showed 20% lower mean latency under burst compared to their previous setup. Another mid-market ecom customer saved 22% on token cost using Redwood Optimize suggestions.

00:09:42 - Maya Chen: Tech highlight — KV cache improvements, kernel swaps for attention, and better prefetch heuristics. Still tuning the quant paths for 4-bit to avoid accuracy regressions.

00:10:05 - David Turner: Finance — quick topline: revenue growth was in line with plan, gross margin improved a little with quantization and Optimize effects. We have runway comfortably into late 2027 assuming plan execution. We will share the complete Q4 numbers in the deck.

00:10:30 - Employee 5 (Speaker): Are we open to strategic partnerships or channel partnerships for regulated industries?

00:10:36 - David Turner: Yes — we're exploring a couple of partnerships that will help with compliance and on-prem packaging. We'll be selective.

00:10:48 - Priya Nair: Roadmap detail: Console will get rollout waves and auto-fallback logic so that if a model variant degrades we'll auto-switch to a compatible variant to keep application up. That is tied to our reliability SLOs and should help customers with zero-downtime expectations.

00:11:12 - Liam O'Connor: On the engineering side, to support that we need better model variant compatibility checks and a small offline testing harness to validate fallbacks before rolling.

00:11:30 - David Turner: Quick note on security/compliance: SOC2 next cycle is scheduled for Q2 audit, we're doing a readiness review in January. For Private customers, the new KMS/HSM integration will be validated in our compliance pack.

00:11:50 - Employee 6 (Speaker): Any changes to expense policy for next year?

00:11:56 - Rachel Singh: Not immediate changes. We'll keep the existing travel and expense thresholds, but will tighten approvals for large discretionary spends.

00:12:10 - David Turner: OK — lightning round of shoutouts. Big kudos to the Optimize team and the infra folks who pushed the kernel work. Also thanks to Solutions EM for supporting pilots.

00:12:28 - Maya Chen: Quick engineering note — we'll be ramping internal load tests next month to exercise the new autoscaling logic; if you see test traffic in staging please don't be alarmed.

00:12:40 - Priya Nair: Demo follow-up: we'll share a short clip of the new rollout canary behavior in the product channel.

00:12:48 - David Turner: Final logistics: offsite in Feb — signups open next week. Deck will be shared after this call. Q's, last minute?

00:12:58 - Employee 7 (Speaker): Any update on docs for Private customers for installation?

00:13:04 - Maya Chen: We're publishing an install guide draft to the private docs repo by 2026-12-07. It's not final but should cover basics and common gotchas for IAM and SAML mapping.

00:13:18 - David Turner: Alright, thanks everyone. We'll wrap up. Recap of action items: David to share deck; Priya to publish roadmap; Maya finalize Private case study; Omar to follow up on pilots; Rachel to send holiday calendar.

00:13:32 - David Turner: Thanks team, happy holidays in advance.

(End of meeting)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard technical terms (K V cache / KV cash, sam-el for SAML), numbers rounded in the summary, some speaker labels generic.
